name: Chefchaouen Blue Medina
shortDescription: Striking blue-washed alleyways nestled in the Rif Mountains.
description: Chefchaouen is famous for its striking blue-washed buildings nestled in the Rif Mountains. Stroll through narrow cobblestone alleys adorned with colorful pottery, handwoven blankets, and blooming plant pots.
whyVisit: Unmatched blue architecture, serene mountain air, and authentic Moroccan craft shops.
bestTimeToVisit: Spring (March to May) & Autumn (September to November)

name: Akchour Waterfalls & God’s Bridge
shortDescription: Natural canyon with emerald pools, waterfalls, and God’s Bridge arch.
description: A spectacular natural canyon with emerald natural pools, lush green foliage, towering cliff walls, and the iconic limestone rock arch known as God’s Bridge.
whyVisit: Breathtaking river trekking, pristine freshwater pools, and mountain canyon scenery.

name: Caves of Hercules (Les Grottes d’Hercule)
shortDescription: Historic cave opening looking out onto the Atlantic Ocean.
description: An archaeological cave complex situated right on the Atlantic coast. The sea opening resembles an inverted map of Africa, making it one of Tangier’s most iconic landmarks.
whyVisit: Mythological origin, ocean view cave opening shaped like Africa, and coastal breeze.

shortDescription: Lush cedar and oak forest reserve in the heart of the Rif.
description: Jbel Bouhachem Natural Reserve protects ancient oak and cedar forests inhabited by Barbary macaques and diverse bird species. Great for eco-tourism and mountain village walks.
whyVisit: Ancient cedar forest, Barbary macaque sightings, quiet trekking paths.
bestTimeToVisit: March to June & September to November

name: Talassemtane National Park
shortDescription: UNESCO biosphere reserve with rare fir trees and deep gorges.
description: Extending across the Rif Mountains near Chefchaouen, Talassemtane features limestone cliffs, deep canyons, and rare Moroccan fir forests found nowhere else on earth.
whyVisit: Endemic flora, dramatic gorge panoramas, wilderness hiking trails.

shortDescription: High mountain peak offering 360-degree Rif views.
description: Jbel Kalti reaches an elevation of nearly 1,900 meters, offering serious hikers a rewarding summit climb through cedar forests to views overlooking Tetouan and Chefchaouen.
whyVisit: Panoramic summit views, challenging summit hike, untouched wilderness.

shortDescription: Coastal mountain summit facing Gibraltar across the sea.

name: Medina of Tetouan UNESCO
shortDescription: Authentic 15th-century Andalusian medina with white fortress walls.
description: One of Morocco's best preserved medinas, Tetouan served as the main point of contact between Morocco and Andalusia. Features artisan guilds, whitewashed houses, and historic gates.
whyVisit: Unspoiled UNESCO heritage, authentic artisan souks, Spanish-Moorish architecture.

name: Kasbah Museum of Tangier
shortDescription: Sultan palace museum of Mediterranean antiquities.
description: Housed in the 17th-century Dar el-Makhzen palace at the highest point of Tangier's Kasbah. Features Roman mosaics from Volubilis, ancient coins, and peaceful Andalusian courtyard gardens.
whyVisit: Royal palace architecture, Roman mosaic floors, sweeping harbor views.

name: Lixus Archaeological Ruins
shortDescription: Ancient Phoenician-Roman city atop a hill overlooking the Loukkos river.
description: One of the oldest continuously inhabited urban centers in North Africa, dating back to 1000 BC. Ruins include a Roman amphitheater, garum fish processing vats, and temples.
whyVisit: Over 3,000 years of history, Roman amphitheater, river valley views.
